memory_candidates.content: When mass-migrating shell test suites onto a shared harness library, a naive diff that counts raw '[FAIL]'-tagged lines per suite output can produce a false-positive regression signal if any suite's own test case legitimately dumps diagnostic output from a live-repo scan (e.g. re-running a real gate/lint against the actual working tree as part of explaining why its own fixture baseline is dirty). That sub-text varies with ambient repo state (deploy-tree freshness, concurrent sibling tasks' untracked files) independent of any change to the suite itself. Use the suite's own authoritative 'Passed: N'/'Failed: N' tally line as ground truth for before/after case-outcome comparison, not a raw tag/line count.

A mechanical shell-boilerplate-collapse migration script that only removes a local pass()/fail()/info() trio and inserts a library source line captures a much smaller net-line-reduction than one that ALSO collapses adjacent boilerplate shapes (a git-aware REPO_ROOT resolution block, a WORKDIR=mktemp+cleanup+trap triplet) onto the same library's helper functions -- the call-site renames themselves change line WIDTH, not line COUNT, so most of a migration's net deletion comes from the structural-block collapses, not the call renames. If a migration's realized net comes in far below a prior tranche's per-suite average, check whether these adjacent patterns were left uncollapsed before accepting the smaller number.

In this sandboxed Claude Code environment, a foreground Bash call running past roughly 180 seconds gets auto-backgrounded by the harness regardless of the declared 'timeout' tool parameter (observed consistently, diverging from the documented 120s-default/600s-ceiling contract) and regardless of periodic heartbeat output. The working pattern for a long-running detached process (e.g. run-all.sh across dozens of suites, or deploy-headless.sh): launch detached with nohup, capture the PID to a file, then poll with a SEQUENCE of short (sleep 100-170s) single-shot 'kill -0 ' checks that each individually return well under the ~180s threshold, reading the log once liveness ends.
